bib.title: Harness-1: Reinforcement Learning for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Harness-1: Reinforcement Learning for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses", Pengcheng Jiang, Zhiyi Shi, Kelly Hong, Xueqiang Xu, Jiashuo Sun, Jimeng Sun, Hammad Bashir, Jiawei Han (UIUC, UC Berkeley, Chroma). Preprint, arXiv:2606.02373v1, 1 Jun 2026 (NeurIPS-style checklist attached).

COVERAGE: All 63 of 63 pages were read, about 194k chars of extraction at /tmp/h1/t.txt. Main text, limitations, the tables in Appendices C to P, the algorithms and prompts, and the NeurIPS checklist were read in full. The case studies (App. Q, pp. 31-58) were read in full for Q.1 and skimmed for Q.2-Q.5, where I read only the outcome lines and summaries. References were skimmed. Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are plots and extracted as numbers only. I did not run the figures script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: A 20B search agent trained with RL inside a stateful harness beats the best open search agent by 11.4 recall points and is competitive with frontier models.
  number: 0.730 average curated recall; +11.4 points over Tongyi DeepResearch 30B
  setup: 8 retrieval benchmarks (web, finance, patents, multi-hop QA). Base model gpt-oss-20b. Results averaged over 3 runs. At most 30 documents returned. Same reranker (Qwen3-Reranker-8B) for all systems. Harness-1 runs 40 turns at temperature 1.0. Frontier models run in the Context-1 harness with a 64-turn cap.
  quote: "Harness-1 is the strongest open retrieval subagent we evaluate, reaching 0.730 average curated recall and improving over the next open subagent, Tongyi DeepResearch 30B, by +11.4 points." Also: "with Opus-4.6 the only frontier retriever ahead on average."
  where: p.7 (Sec 3.2), Table 2 p.6, abstract
- Claim: Removing the harness at inference time, with the trained policy unchanged, cuts recall. Disabling all mechanisms is worse than disabling any one.
  number: Recall 0.584 to 0.513 (-12.2% relative); final-answer recall 0.667 to 0.624 (-6.4%)
  setup: Same trained checkpoint, 100 paired BrowseComp+ test queries, no retraining, one mechanism disabled per row.
  quote: "With every Harness-1 mechanism off simultaneously ... Recall drops to 0.513 and FA recall to 0.624 — a larger relative Recall drop than any single ablation."
  where: Table 3 p.8; App M.2 p.28
- Claim: Single ablations (relative change in final-answer recall). Importance tags -7.9%, sentence-BM25 compression -7.0%, auto-seed -6.4%, evidence graph hidden -5.4%, verify off -3.9%, review_docs off -3.9%. Content dedup off is the only one that helps (+1.6%).
  number: see list; recall deltas -4.1, +0.2, -0.3, -2.6, -3.1, +2.4, +4.6 (%)
  setup: BrowseComp+, 100 queries, inference-time ablation. No error bars. Dedup "helps" because MinHash dedup (Jaccard 0.85) sometimes merges two near-duplicate gold documents.
  quote: "Six of seven mechanisms produce clean FA-recall drops (−3.9% to −7.9% relative)"; "Content dedup is the only ablation that nominally helps (+4.6% Recall, +1.6% FA, both relative)."
  where: p.8, Table 3; App M.1 pp.26-28
- Claim: When a state mechanism is removed, the policy reverts to wide, shallow, search-only behaviour. It stops reading and verifying.
  number: search_corpus share up 3-7 points; read_document and verify down 2-6x. Example: with importance tags removed, search_corpus is 94.1% of actions.
  setup: Paired queries that the full system solves (FA recall >= 0.5) and the ablated one fails (FA recall = 0). The paper reports 9-15 such queries per ablation.
  quote: "search_corpus rises by 3–7 points and read_document/verify drop 2–6×."
  where: p.8; App M p.26
- Claim: Gains are larger on held-out benchmarks than on source-family benchmarks.
  number: held-out mean +17.0 recall points vs source-family mean +7.9 (2.2x), measured against Context-1
  setup: Held-out: LongSealQA +32.8, Seal0QA +18.4, FRAMES +7.2, HotpotQA +9.5. Source-family: BC+ +6.2, Web +9.8, Patents +3.3, SEC +12.2. SFT used BC+, Web, Patents and SEC. RL used SEC only. The held-out four were never trained on.
  quote: "This is a 2.2× larger gain on the benchmarks furthest from any training data"
  where: p.7, Fig 3. The text calls the baseline "closest open baseline", and the figure caption says Context-1. Check which when citing.
- Claim: Without a tool-diversity reward, RL collapses to search-only behaviour. With it, final recall is higher.
  number: Without it, diversity falls from ~6 to ~3.5 and curated recall plateaus at ~0.53. With it, diversity holds at ~4.30 and recall reaches ~0.60.
  setup: Two RL runs from the same SFT checkpoint, differing only in w_div. Read from Fig 5, 80 steps. Single run each, no seeds.
  quote: "Tool diversity falls from ∼6 to ∼3.5, and curated recall plateaus at ∼0.53." and "final curated recall is higher, reaching ∼0.60."
  where: p.9, Fig 5
- Claim: A fixed frontier model gains from a richer harness with no RL.
  number: GPT-5.4 curated recall 0.511 (naive search-add), 0.807 (Context-1 harness), 0.849 (Harness-1 harness). Final-answer recall 0.612, 0.821, 0.876.
  setup: GPT-5.4 on three in-domain benchmarks. The paper does not name them here. Fig 7.
  quote: "Curated Recall jumps from 0.511 (naive) to 0.807 (Context-1) to 0.849 (Harness-1)"; "A +4.2 point recall gain is available to GPT-5.4 simply by switching ... without any RL training."
  where: App P p.30
- Claim: The remaining gap to Opus-4.6 is selection, not discovery.
  number: BC+ final-answer recall 0.658 vs 0.736 for Opus-4.6, with similar trajectory recall
  setup: BrowseComp+, Table 2. The table itself lists 0.667 for Harness-1 BC+ FA recall, so the text figure 0.658 and the table disagree.
  quote: "final-answer recall (0.658 vs. 0.736), despite similar trajectory recall, is therefore mainly a selection gap rather than a discovery gap."
  where: p.9 vs Table 2 p.6
- Claim: Little training data is needed because behaviour sits in the interface.
  number: 899 filtered SFT trajectories (about 26K per-turn datums) plus RL on 3,453 SEC queries, 4,352 unique items. Context-1 used over 8K SFT tasks and 9,159 RL queries. Search-R1 used 221,328 RL rows.
  setup: Counts unique queries, not tokens or rollouts. RL ran 80 steps of 1,024 rollouts, about 82K rollouts in total.
  quote: "Harness-1 moves much of the behavioral prior into the stateful interface, allowing small SFT and focused RL to transfer."
  where: p.8, Fig 4; Tables 5-6, pp.18-19
- Claim: Better curated sets raise downstream answer accuracy across four frozen generators.
  number: none stated in text (bar values in Fig 6 only, e.g. BC+ about 0.65 for Harness-1 vs about 0.51-0.59 for Context-1 under some generators; read from plot, unreliable)
  setup: GPT-5.4, Sonnet-4.6, Opus-4.6 and Kimi-K2.5 see only the query and curated documents. Judge is GPT-5.4 at T=0.
  quote: "Harness-1's curated sets dominate the open subagents in the reported modular RAG settings."
  where: App O p.29

Design facts worth keeping (harness = policy/environment split)
- The harness holds a two-tier working memory. The prompt tier holds the candidate pool, curated set with importance tags, evidence graph, verification records, search history and budget marker. The outer tier holds full text, reachable via review_docs/read_document.
- Curated set cap is 30. Eviction is by lowest importance. Auto-seed puts the top 8 results of the first search into the set at "fair".
- Context budget is 30,720 prompt tokens of 32,768, with a 5-pass progressive degradation. The curated set and recent memory are cut last. The agent is told "wrap up above 75% and call end_search above 90%".
- Observations: sentence-BM25 compression keeps K=4 sentences. Dedup is MinHash-LSH, 64 permutations, 5-gram shingles, threshold 0.85.
- Reward: set quality (F-beta, beta=2) + trajectory recall + answer terms + diversity (0.15, target 6 tools) - turn penalty. Empty curated set gets -0.2. Terminal reward only, no KL, 40-turn cap.

LIMITS
- The authors' limits: scope is evidence-seeking retrieval. Breadth-oriented research, report generation, abstention and adversarial web are out of scope. The evidence graph is regex entity extraction. verify is an LLM proxy for entailment. BM25 compression may drop discourse-dependent context. Benchmarks are small, and qrels have near-duplicates and gaps.
- Checklist item 7 answers "No" on error bars: "We do not report formal confidence intervals or significance tests for all main comparisons." The ablation uses only 100 BC+ queries. Table 2 is averaged over 3 runs, but no spread is shown.
- The harness includes programmatic nudges ([ACTION REQUIRED], [WARN], [TIP], [NEXT]) that are part of the "harness mass" ablated. The authors say these "are not part of the trained policy's intrinsic capability", so some of the gain is hard-coded prompting.
- Frontier baselines run in Context-1's harness and not their own. Search-R1 and Tongyi use their own harnesses plus a shared reranker.
- The paper is about a retrieval subagent with a 40-turn, 32K-context episode. It does not test multi-session or multi-hour work. Applying it to the note's session-lifecycle material is an analogy. "Long-horizon" here means a long search episode.
- Single RL run per configuration. Teacher is GPT-5.4. RL on SEC only.

BUILDS ON: Context-1 (Bashir, Hong, Jiang, Shi, Chroma, Mar 2026, self-editing search agent). SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024) and Xia et al. (2024, 2025) for interface effects. ReAct (Yao 2022), IRCoT (Trivedi 2023), Active RAG (Jiang 2023). Search-R1 (Jin 2025), DeepRetrieval, s3 (Jiang 2025). CISPO (MiniMax-M1, Chen 2025). Context rot (Hong, Troynikov, Huber, Chroma 2025). Harness engineering (Lopopolo 2026; Martin et al., Anthropic "Scaling managed agents", Apr 2026). MemGPT (Packer 2024) and Mem1 (Zhou 2025) for memory. Automated harness work: AutoHarness, Meta-Harness, Harbor.

CODE: No code listings. Useful verbatim fragments:
- Rendered working memory header: "== Working Memory (summarising turns 0--n) ==" (App F, p.20)
- Budget marker: "[Context: 19,840/30,720]" (Fig 2, p.3)
- Verify sub-prompt: "You are a strict document verifier. ... answer only yes or no, followed by a rationale of at most 20 words. Answer yes only if the document directly supports every part of the claim." (App I.2, p.23)
- Agent prompt state rule: "very high requires prior verification." (App I.1, p.22-23)

FIGURES (captions from extraction; images not viewed)
- Fig 2 (p.3): harness overview. Policy actions on the left, harness state (pool, graph, curated set, verification cache, compression) on the right, one state interface for teacher, SFT, RL and eval. Best single picture of the policy/environment split.
- Fig 3 (p.7): per-benchmark recall gain over Context-1; held-out +17.0 vs source +7.9.
- Fig 5 (p.9): training curves with and without the diversity reward; shows collapse.
- Fig 7 (p.30): same GPT-5.4 under three harnesses.
- Table 3 (p.8): the ablation table, most useful for the note.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean text. Plots come out as scattered numbers, so Fig 1 and 6 values are not reliable and I did not quote them. Discrepancy: the text gives BC+ final-answer recall as 0.658 while Table 2 shows 0.667. The Fig 3 caption says gains are over Context-1, while the body text says "closest open baseline", and Tongyi is named as the next-best average. No embedded instructions in the PDF. For the target note: the paper's relevance to note 06 is thin, since the mechanism is state externalization in a retrieval episode, supporting "progress lives outside the window" and "re-test harness components per model". It does not address multi-session handoffs, compaction vs reset, or context anxiety. The note (06-long-horizon-execution.md) does not currently cite it. I did not edit anything.
